stem:
A 45-year-old man with primary hyperaldosteronism has hypertension and a low serum potassium concentration.

His elevated aldosterone acts on principal cells of the collecting duct to produce which of the following changes?

options.label: A
options.text: Fewer sodium channels, so less sodium and water are recovered
options.misconception: The hormone's effect on sodium handling is being stated backward.
options.explanation: Aldosterone increases, not decreases, sodium-channel production; excess aldosterone therefore expands volume (hypertension) rather than shrinking it.

options.label: B
options.text: Insertion of aquaporin water channels into the apical membrane
options.misconception: ADH's signature action is being attributed to aldosterone.
options.explanation: Aquaporin insertion is controlled by ADH; aldosterone builds sodium/potassium channels and pumps, and water then follows the recovered sodium passively.

options.label: C
options.text: Suppression of potassium secretion, conserving serum potassium
options.misconception: The direction of potassium handling is being reversed.
options.explanation: Aldosterone promotes potassium loss: as the Na+/K+ pump recovers Na+, K+ moves the opposite way into the forming urine, which is why hyperaldosteronism causes hypokalemia.

options.label: D
options.text: Conversion of angiotensin I into active angiotensin II
options.misconception: An upstream enzyme's role is being assigned to the steroid's target cells.
options.explanation: Angiotensin-converting enzyme from the lungs activates angiotensin II; principal cells respond to aldosterone by manufacturing channels and pumps.

options.label: E
options.text: More sodium and potassium channels plus more Na+/K+ ATPase pumps
options.misconception: None; aldosterone upregulates the whole sodium-recovery/potassium-secretion machinery.
options.explanation: Aldosterone stimulates principal cells to manufacture luminal Na+ and K+ channels and basal Na+/K+ ATPase pumps; more Na+ is recovered (with water following) while more K+ is pumped into the forming urine, explaining his hypertension and hypokalemia.

context: Learning objective: state aldosterone's principal-cell program. Aldosterone induces luminal Na+/K+ channels and basal Na+/K+ ATPase, increasing Na+ (and water) recovery and K+ secretion.
